logline: A freelance filmmaker discovers her old digital camera can record footage from the future, revealing a terrifying premonition and a warning not to trust her producer, Daniel, as she races against an impending disaster.

scenes_scheduled.heading: INT. MAYA'S APARTMENT - NIGHT
scenes_scheduled.summary: Maya, a freelance filmmaker, discovers her old digital camera mysteriously recorded footage from "TOMORROW" showing a future version of herself giving a dire warning.
vfx_requirements: Camera screen displaying 'recording' indicator and timestamp
scenes_scheduled.notes: Ensure camera screen is clean for VFX compositing. Subtle rain effect via VFX for atmosphere.

scenes_scheduled.heading: ON THE LAPTOP SCREEN - VIDEO
scenes_scheduled.summary: The video shows a future Maya in a ransacked apartment, urgently warning present-day Maya not to go to the station tomorrow, not to take the 11:47 train, and not to trust Daniel.
vfx_requirements: Screen composite of Future Maya in ransacked apartment
VFX/Set dressing for overturned furniture and shattered window in footage
Flickering light effect on screen footage
scenes_scheduled.notes: Requires significant VFX integration for the laptop screen footage; ensure laptop screen is clean for compositing. Coordinate set dressing with VFX for the 'ransacked' look within the video footage.

scenes_scheduled.heading: INT. MAYA'S APARTMENT - LATER
scenes_scheduled.summary: Maya receives a message and call from Daniel, who reveals he also saw the future video and instructs her to destroy the camera, as the apartment lights flicker and the camera begins recording again.
vfx_requirements: Subtle flickering effect on apartment lights
Blinking red recording light on digital camera
scenes_scheduled.notes: Practical flickering lights combined with VFX for enhancement. Ensure camera recording light is clear for VFX.

required_equipment: Basic lighting package (LED panels, stands, dimmers)
production_notes: VFX Supervisor to be on set for screen capture requirements and flickering light integration.
Ensure all digital props (camera, laptop, phone) have clean screens for VFX compositing.
Prepare for rapid set dressing adjustments if apartment states change during the shoot.
safety_and_logistics: Standard apartment filming safety protocols to be observed.
Ensure clear pathways for crew and equipment within the apartment.

scenes_scheduled.heading: INT. TRAIN STATION - NIGHT
scenes_scheduled.summary: At the train station, Maya sees a live recording of herself with a mysterious figure behind her. She boards the train with Daniel, sees a future of the train derailing on her camera, and barely escapes before the train departs, prompting a "TIMELINE UPDATED." message.
vfx_requirements: Mysterious, shadowy figure composited behind Maya within the camera screen's live feed
Complex VFX composite of train derailing footage onto camera screen
Clear 'TIMELINE UPDATED.' message composite on camera screen
Seamless integration of partial train car set piece with green screen backgrounds if needed
Digital passengers/crowd enhancement if required for wide shots
scenes_scheduled.notes: VFX Supervisor essential on set for all greenscreen and screen composite elements. Ensure partial train car set piece is ready and dressed. Coordinate closely with dedicated Railway Safety Officer for all activities. Plan for crowd control and management, even during off-peak hours. Prepare for quick egress from location in case of unexpected railway operations.

required_equipment: Specialized grip equipment for train environment (if permitted)
Lighting package adapted for station environment
production_notes: Prioritize early engagement with railway authorities to understand specific permit requirements, lead times, and associated costs.
Pre-production walk-through with railway operators and dedicated safety officer is critical.
Carefully plan camera movements and equipment usage to comply with restrictions on tripods, artificial lighting, and yellow line rules on platforms.
Budget for comprehensive liability insurance that specifically covers filming on railway property.
Prepare a clear production concept and script breakdown for review by railway operators during the permit application process.
safety_and_logistics: Confirm filming permit requirements with the selected station/railway operator, anticipating significant lead times and fees.
Confirm equipment restrictions with the selected location authority, especially regarding tripods, artificial lighting, and obstructing pathways.
Confirm with the selected station/railway operator the rules governing filming near platforms, tracks, and approaching trains. Follow all operator safety instructions.
A dedicated safety officer with experience in railway environments is required on set.
Plan all practical train station filming during off-peak hours (likely late night/early morning).
Secure comprehensive liability insurance with specific clauses covering filming on railway property, as this is a mandatory requirement.
Conduct mandatory safety briefings for all crew members accessing railway property.
All equipment on platforms must be secured/weighted to prevent movement.
Confirm any railway-specific safety training required for key crew members.
Confirm public access restrictions and management strategy during filming to avoid disruptions.
